label: GPT-6.1 Sol
output:
Tolu, me o 😂 Biology 100L here, and Medicine and Surgery was what I applied for too. I scored 251 in JAMB 2025 and got Biology at a federal uni here in Lagos. So when you said you checked your portal and started crying, I understood that one very well.

The day I saw Biology on my portal, I locked myself inside my cousin’s room in Surulere and cried. I didn’t eat. In my head, it was already Medicine or nothing, so seeing another course felt like everything had scattered. My mum didn’t even help matters because she was still telling people in church that I was studying Medicine for like two months 😭 I had to beg her to stop. Having to explain “actually, it’s Biology” every time was painful enough without getting fresh congratulations for Medicine.

So first, you’re not ungrateful for being upset. You can appreciate getting admission and still be disappointed that it wasn’t what you wanted. Both can be true. But please try not to make the final decision while you’re still in that first shock.

Let me answer the transfer part properly, because that was one of the first things I wanted to know too.

**Transfer to Medicine is real, but it is not automatic at all.** What our level adviser told us here is that you need a CGPA of at least **4.5 out of 5**, AND there must be space in Medicine. Those are two separate things. Getting the CGPA doesn’t mean they must take you.

According to her, about six people moved into Medicine from the whole faculty last year, and she thinks over 40 people applied. I’m saying “according to her” because I didn’t personally count the applicants or see everybody’s records. But that was what she told us, and it should give you an idea of why “just enter and transfer” is not something to build your whole plan around.

She also said we would need to meet the Medicine cut-offs in JAMB and post-UTME. So your 268 by itself doesn’t settle whether you’re eligible. I don’t know your school’s cut-offs or what you scored in post-UTME, and I don’t want to come here and confidently give you wrong information. You need to check both, plus whatever other conditions your own school has.

That’s where I disagree with both replies small. Kingsley saying transfer is a myth is not correct as a general statement. Not knowing anybody who transferred doesn’t mean nobody transfers. But Favour saying you should just read hard is also making it sound simpler than it is. You can read hard and still fall short of the required CGPA. You can even meet the academic requirements and there may not be space.

My own first-semester CGPA is **4.31**. Not 4.5. I’m still trying. I’m telling you the actual figure because I don’t want to sound like somebody who has already cracked the whole thing and is now giving motivational speeches. I came in wanting Medicine too, but wanting it badly has not automatically given me the grades.

And 100L Biology is not only Biology o. We’re doing BIO 101, CHM 101, PHY 101, MTH 101 and GST. Physics and Maths are the ones dealing with people. If your plan is to aim for transfer, you have to take all the courses seriously, not just the ones you enjoy or the ones that sound related to Medicine. Those other results will still enter your CGPA.

For the practical side, also prepare for expenses outside whatever school fees you’ve already seen. My lab coat was ₦6,500, dissecting kit was ₦9,000, and practical manual was extra. Your own prices may be different, but I’m mentioning it because this is part of being inside the course too. It’s not just lectures and waiting for a transfer form.

Now, is Biology a bad course? Honestly, no. I’m enjoying parts of it much more than I expected, especially genetics and cell biology. That surprised me because I entered with my mind still on Medicine, so I wasn’t exactly giving Biology a fair chance at first.

Our first BIO practical, we dissected toads. One guy in my group fainted, and I was fine 😂 But beyond that, I was actually interested in what we were doing. That was the day I first thought, “Wait, I actually like this thing.” It didn’t mean all my disappointment disappeared or that I suddenly forgot Medicine. It just meant Biology itself wasn’t the punishment I had made it in my head.

That’s my experience, though. I won’t use it to promise that you’ll love it once you enter. You may enjoy it, or you may still strongly prefer Medicine. Biology and Medicine are different courses, and it’s fair to be honest about which one you want. But don’t conclude that Biology is bad only because it wasn’t your first choice.

For me, the important question before accepting would be: **if the transfer doesn’t happen, can I see myself continuing in Biology?** You don’t have to already be excited about it, but if your answer is “never, under any circumstances,” please take that seriously. Accepting only because you believe you’ll definitely leave after 100L is a risky plan.

On rewriting, I don’t think it’s wrong either. If Medicine is genuinely what you want and you’re ready to prepare again, that is a valid choice. I just wish people would stop saying “one year is nothing” as if they’re the ones who will live that year for you. Staying home and trying again can be hard, especially when people keep asking questions and your mates are in school.

My secondary school classmate Ifeoma rejected Pharmacy to rewrite for Medicine. She has written JAMB two more times and she’s still at home. I’m not saying that to frighten you or to say she made a foolish decision. I’m saying rewriting is another attempt, not a guaranteed Medicine admission. Just as accepting Biology doesn’t guarantee a transfer, rejecting it doesn’t guarantee that next year will go exactly how you want.

Before your acceptance deadline, please go to your faculty or department and ask for the **exact transfer rules in your own school**. If they direct you to another office, follow it up. Ask whether Biology students can apply for MBBS transfer, the required CGPA, the JAMB and post-UTME conditions, how spaces affect selection, and when applications happen. If there’s a written policy you can read, even better. Also ask how many people actually transferred recently, if they can tell you.

Don’t just trust forum people, including me. I can tell you what our adviser said and what my own first semester has been like. I cannot use my school’s information to guarantee what will happen in yours.

And please ask yourself one uncomfortable question privately: do you want to study and practise Medicine, or do you mainly want to be “Doctor” because that’s what your parents have always wanted? No insult intended at all. After my own church announcement situation, I know how family expectations can enter your head until it’s hard to separate their dream from yours. You can genuinely want Medicine too, but you deserve to know your own reason.

So I won’t tell you “accept it jor,” and I won’t tell you “rewrite, no two ways.” Find out the rules first. Then decide whether you’re willing to study Biology even if transfer fails, or whether you’re willing to face another admission attempt and its uncertainty.

Sorry, this got long, but you asked for somebody inside it 😂 Please eat something and give yourself small breathing space. This is a serious decision, yes, but Biology on your portal is not the end of your life. Whatever you choose, you haven’t failed at 19 because admission didn’t go the way you planned.
